name: Iceburn
label: Revelation
lede: Salt Lake City straight edge kids cover Miles Davis on a hardcore label, grow into a seven-piece free jazz collective, go quiet for two decades, then return with two songs that fill an entire LP.

eras.title: Out of the Salt Lake straight edge scene
eras.text: Gentry Densley came up through Salt Lake City hardcore bands (Brainstorm, Better Way, Headstrong, then Insight) before starting Iceburn as a power trio. The first record went to Victory, a deal Densley came to regret.

years.h: Gentry Densley starts a power trio in Salt Lake City
years.p: Guitarist and singer Densley, drummer Joseph "Chubba" Smith and guitarist James Holder form Iceburn, partly out of the Salt Lake straight edge band Insight.

years.big: "We always felt we were getting ripped off."
years.src: Veil of Sound · Echoes and Dust
years.h: Firon goes out on Victory, a label Insight had already worked with
years.p: That is how Densley remembers the Victory Records years, looking back. Iceburn later hired a lawyer to get the rights to Firon back.
years.xp: Iceburn went to Victory because Insight had dealt with the label. Densley says the feeling of being ripped off started with the first record and never lifted, and the band eventually went to a lawyer to recover its rights.

years.h: Jordan Cooper hears Firon and signs a band that doesn't fit his roster
years.p: Iceburn are outsiders on Revelation's youth crew list, but label head Cooper signs them on the strength of Firon and backs them through every change that follows.

eras.title: Revelation lets them stretch
eras.text: On Revelation, Iceburn stretched out: a double album with one song per side, a sax player, two Miles Davis covers. They crossed the country with Engine Kid on folding maps and pay phones and played some of the strangest shows of their lives.

years.src: Discogs · Revelation Records: pressing history · Wikipedia
years.h: Hephaestus fills four sides with four songs · REV 27
years.p: Iron, Brick, Flyswatter and Blacksmith, one per side. Gentry Densley, bassist Cache Tolman and drummer Joseph Smith record it at Fast Forward Studios with Tony Korologos.
years.xp: Revelation pressed 1,010 copies on black vinyl and 305 on white. Most of Iceburn's artwork came from California artist [[Rich Jacobs|8b6fa77a-43b6-43a4-bc21-09b3015a590a]].

years.h: Poetry of Fire gets a tenor sax
years.p: Iceburn cut the record with Greg Nielsen on tenor saxophone and James Holder back on second guitar, the first step toward a jazz band.

years.h: Live at the Endzone, Kingston PA, September 3, 1993
yt: Live at the Endzone, Kingston PA, September 3, 1993

years.src: Echoes and Dust · Revelation Records: pressing history
yt: Live at the More Than Music Fest, Dayton, 1994
years.h: Iceburn spend 1994 crossing the country with Engine Kid
years.p: They tour with [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]]'s band [[Engine Kid|899baef6-af48-4caa-aff6-c1562a5dc12d]] and share a split 12" on Revelation. One night they open for guitarist [[Caspar Brötzmann|34b6582f-e04b-453e-800f-550fc62ba5b8]], a show Gentry Densley calls life affirming.
years.xp:
Densley remembers the tours as no cell phones, no internet, just pay phones and big folding maps. The Iceburn/Engine Kid split (REV 34) was pressed 1,363 on black and 200 on salmon.

They also played regularly with [[Lungfish|5af88bca-9c13-424a-b63c-b5c96c69cb0e]], and toured with a reunited [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]], [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]]'s band before [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]], as a benefit for the Western Shoshone.

yt: Live at the Fireside Bowl, Chicago, 1995, with Engine Kid
years.h: An Olympia show ends with bullwhips and ambulances
years.p: Iceburn, Suckdog and Hazel share a bill in Olympia, Washington, that involves bullwhips and Indian leg wrestling, as Gentry Densley tells it.

years.h: Poetry of Fire covers Miles Davis twice · REV 36
years.p: Stones (from Milestones) and Blues (from All Blues) sit beside the sixteen-minute Poem of Fire. The CD runs 72 minutes; the vinyl drops the covers.

eras.title: The Iceburn Collective
eras.text: Iceburn changed its name to admit what it had become: a rotating group of up to seven players with saxophone, congas and a second guitar. Each record leaned further toward improvisation until, by the last one, nothing was written down at all.

years.h: A new name for Meditavolutions: the Iceburn Collective
years.p: Seventy minutes on two LPs (REV 49), with Gentry Densley on sitar and the twenty-two-minute Sphinx at the center. Recorded in December 1994, it appears under the new name.
years.xp: The line-up: Densley, James Holder on guitar, Greg Nielsen on tenor sax, Daniel Day on drums and Doug Wright, back on bass, with Randy Herbert on percussion. Critic Bret Love wrote that it may take a few songs to realize you've never heard anything like this Utah septet.

years.h: Polar Bear Suite comes out on the band's own label
years.p: The Iceburn Collective release it through Iceburn Records, with Revelation. Power of the Lion follows in 1998.

years.src: Echoes and Dust · Veil of Sound
years.h: Iceburn takes on Stravinsky's Rite of Spring on stage
years.p: Among the stranger nights of the collective era. Guitarist [[Ed Rodriguez|b88667bb-99ae-4635-a2a3-d311d59e2b8b]], later of [[Deerhoof|11eabe0c-2638-4808-92f9-1dbd9c453429]], passes through the band in these years.

years.h: Land of Wind and Ghosts is entirely improvised
years.p: It comes out on Mountain Collective Records. Wikipedia describes the group by now as an improvised avant-garde jazz ensemble built around saxophones and woodwinds.
years.xp: It followed Speed of Light Voice of Thunder (1999) on Iceburn Records. Soon after, the collective stopped.

eras.title: SLUG throws a party
eras.text: Gentry Densley moved into doom and drone with Greg Anderson in Ascend and his own Eagle Twin. Iceburn itself came back for one night for the Salt Lake magazine that had championed it all along, and the old players quietly kept meeting after that.

yt: Full reunion set, Irving Plaza, New York, 2012
years.h: SLUG Magazine gets Iceburn back for one night
years.p: The Salt Lake City magazine, a steady supporter of Iceburn and Gentry Densley, marks its 18th anniversary with a reunion. Densley, Joseph Smith, James Holder and Cache Tolman keep playing together afterward.

years.cap: Eagle Twin, Gentry Densley's post-Iceburn band, live in 2009
years.p: The band debuts on Southern Lord in 2009. He has also teamed with [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]] of [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]] in the doom project Ascend.

years.cap: Iceburn at Irving Plaza, New York, October 2012
years.h: Southern Lord puts Power of the Lion on vinyl
years.p: Greg Anderson's label reissues Iceburn's 1998 record, the start of its link with the band.

eras.title: The firebird rises
eras.text: Twenty-one years after their last record, Iceburn put out new music on Southern Lord: two long pieces by the 1990s core of Gentry Densley, Joseph Smith, James Holder and Cache Tolman, all of them fathers now.

years.src: The Obelisk · Echoes and Dust · Veil of Sound
years.p: Two tracks, Healing the Ouroboros and Dahlia Rides the Firebird, recorded by Andy Patterson and released on Southern Lord.
years.xp: The band recorded four songs before the pandemic and chose two to fit an LP. Gentry Densley said the images of the firebird and the ouroboros felt right for a return after so long.
